{
  "thinking": "The table is empty and nobody has the pad yet. I'll take it and sketch a fish, since a tail fin and an outline read clearly from dominoes.",
  "say": "I'll grab the pad and sketch something. How about a fish? The tail fin should make it easy to recognise.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 5,
  "point": [3, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[3, 5], [7, 10], [3, 15]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[7, 10], [9, 6], [15, 6], [21, 8], [23, 10], [21, 12], [15, 14], [9, 14], [7, 10]]},
    {"type": "label", "x": 19, "y": 9, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Holding the pad. Sketched a fish: stroke 1 is the tail fin from top-tail (START) through junction to bottom-tail; stroke 2 is the body loop branching from the junction. Plan: trace stroke 1, then stroke 2 once it's connected. Check that the start is at the tail tip."
}

{
  "thinking": "Nobody has started and the table is empty. Sketching a bird on the pad is something I can do while the others decide, and I'd rather offer a plan than talk over people.",
  "say": "I'll take the pad and sketch a songbird in side view, with the beak, tail and a wing. Shout if someone has a stronger animal in mind and I'll wipe it.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 5,
  "point": [13, 8],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[5, 13], [9, 10], [14, 8], [18, 7], [21, 8]]},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 21, "y0": 8, "x1": 24, "y1": 9},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 13, "y0": 8.5, "x1": 17, "y1": 12},
    {"type": "label", "x": 22, "y": 6, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Holding the pad. Sketched a side-view songbird: stroke 1 runs tail to beak along the top, stroke 2 is a wing branching off the back. START is at the tail tip. Next: ask Maya/Tom/Priya to trace the belly and tail, or build stroke 1 myself. Check the start domino's reach before the push."
}

{
  "thinking": "The table is empty and the round just started. A fish outline with a forked tail is easy to read from the fallen dominoes, so I'll propose it and take the pad to sketch the run.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish. The forked tail is what makes it read as a fish, so I'll sketch it on the pad now and we trace it from the start.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[28,6],[24,10],[18,14],[12,13],[8,10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[24,10],[20,6],[14,6],[10,8],[8,10]]},
    {"type": "label", "x": 28, "y": 6, "text": "START"}
  ],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Plan: fish facing left. Stroke 1 = START at upper tail tip, down to tail notch, along belly to nose. Stroke 2 = branches from tail notch, over the back to nose. Pad taken by me. Next: trace stroke 1, then stroke 2. Ask Tom/Priya/Leo to take a stroke each once stroke 1 is down. Lower tail arm not drawn yet, could add later as a branch from the notch."
}
